laws.summary: AI is an independent first-class ability group and must remain the only public AI owner.
AI child capabilities represent provider/runtime channels; business task routing is AI-owned and must not replace child ids.
AI may reason and return structured results only; it may not execute actions or side effects.
local-ai-runtime is an internal execution boundary under AI ownership and must not become a second public AI system.
paid and future API AI children are visible but disabled by policy and must fail closed.
AI outputs must be cleaned before persistence and must not leak AI runtime contracts into Forensics public ownership.
AI keeps a single public contract and does not leak child, adapter, prompt, or legacy internals.
ai-capability inspector is the only enforcement owner for AI topology, runtime pipeline, prompt truth, and anti-escape checks.
AI owns the Prompt Contract Registry; prompt execution must resolve by promptContractId/version/catalog, never by hardcoded prompt text.
Prompt contracts must declare full governed metadata and must be hashable, strict, and audit-proof.
Prompt contracts may guide reasoning only and must not command actions, bypass security, or make final mission decisions.
AI runtime must resolve prompt execution by promptContractId and execute a governed runtime pipeline with typed failures.
AI timeout, cancellation, idempotency, concurrency, and circuit breaker state must be governed and proof-backed.
AI result proof must be complete, chain-linked, raw-output-backed, and impossible to fake as success.
AI output boundary must recursively block action authority, browser authority, Forensics authority, and command authority.
inspector plus generated artifacts plus audit runner is the only enforcement chain.
Map Prompt Contract Governance must be enforced by AST, schema, and negative proof.
Prompt contract and map binding drift is audit-blocking.
GrassEye uses one fixed ability-group constitution and one execution chain.
every ability group owns one public contract and one child-boundary catalog.
Commander, Nerve Bus, and Orchestration each have one fixed authority boundary.
runtime proof minimum fields are fixed across every governed execution.
every governed execution must leave evidence, log, and trace.
ability groups must keep hard boundaries and topology must reflect ownership.
Capability Catalog is a generated read model, not a new owner.
AI-generated map authoring must use the governed capability catalog.
active source files must stay atomic and must not exceed Code Purity Phase 3.5 file-size limits.
touched oversized files must be split before new logic is added.
functions must stay small, shallow, and single-purpose.
classes and objects must not become god objects.
owner boundaries must be counted at real capability-owner granularity.
imports and exports must not create hidden broad ownership or barrel laundering.
files must have one role and must not mix schema, runtime, validation, execution, persistence, and decision responsibilities.
dead code, fake runtime paths, mocks, placeholders, and temporary bypasses must not survive in active source truth.
refactors must reduce ownership, file size, complexity, and active paths rather than adding compatibility bridges.
disaster files must be identified, blocked, and physically split before meaningful feature debugging continues.
all active code-purity laws must be proven by real enforcement, generated audit artifacts, runner execution, and negative proof.
type-safety and escape hatches must not be used to bypass purity enforcement.
code-purity enforcement must produce inventories, remediation queues, and physical split plans.
code-purity remediation must use physical deletion and physical splitting, not cosmetic renaming.
code-topology is a capability-group-governance child sub-contract for canonical roots, not an active owner.
feature and support paths are consumers or boundaries, not owners.
retired feature roots must be physically deleted after migration.
Forensics Persistence must use one clean internal topology and must physically delete old runtime/store roots.
Commander Console is the only owner of human command entry, review disposition entry, and command-facing operator dashboard read models.
Commander Console reads governed truth only and must not create a second runtime truth or preserve old workbench demo truth.
Commander Console must keep hard boundaries away from browser, platform-action, AI runtime, and storage internals.
Commander Console may import governed map packages and expose task-template UX without becoming map execution or activation truth.
Commander Console must own one canonical root, one child catalog, and zero compat bridges.
Commander Console may read Forensics truth only through governed read models and must not import store internals.
Forensics Persistence is the only final evidence-ledger owner and must not be bypassed by local-data, runtime, workbench, Commander, AI, or action abilities.
child abilities must be persistence behaviors and every child must write exactly one governed Forensics record type.
Forensics writes and links records only; it must not reason, verify, decide, act, or reconstruct business truth.
Forensics public contract must be Forensics-native and must not leak legacy business or runtime type sovereignty.
every Forensics record and result must preserve the full execution chain and must be replayable.
storage must be a generic record-store port and old store ownership must stay outside the canonical Forensics root.
Forensics writes must be policy-gated, integrity-gated, idempotent, and append-safe.
Forensics enforcement must be AST/symbol/import-graph based and connected to runner and negative proof.
Geometry Guard is a coordinate safety gate only.
Geometry Guard public contract must stay clean and independent.
Geometry Guard validates mappings and bounds from governed evidence only.
Geometry Guard must consume evidence and ports, not browser ownership.
Geometry Guard enforcement closes through the owner inspector only.
local-ai-runtime is an AI child sub-contract and internal runtime adapter, not an active owner.
model-role routing must stay explicit and traceable.
prompts are governed task contracts, not hidden strings.
model configuration is local, role-based, and no-fallback.
legacy LocalAi contracts are bridge-only and must not escape back into AI public ownership.
local-app-shell is a commander-console child sub-contract for local shell form, not an active owner.
shell layers must stay separated from command and mission truth.
desktop packaging is a wrapper, not a second architecture.
startup is a bounded local bootstrap path.
browser-session is an Open child sub-contract for real-Chrome reuse, not an active owner.
local-persistence-schema is a Forensics child sub-contract for schema truth, not an active owner.
schema terms must align to ForensicsRecordEnvelope and artifact refs rather than legacy domain objects.
Map plugins are declarative data packages consumed by Orchestration, not runtime code or child capabilities.
Map plugins must enter quarantine on import and cannot become active without validation and approval.
Map plugins must declare full package governance metadata and own their package schemas.
Map plugins must never carry executable payloads or direct ability control.
Map plugins expose task-template UX while keeping internal runtime identifiers private in ordinary mode.
AI-generated maps are draft-only until validation and human approval.
Map package enforcement closes through the map-plugin-package inspector and audit runner scripts.
Map packages may reference prompt contracts but must not embed raw prompt logic or hidden runtime instructions.
AI-generated map packages must be authored against governed catalogs.
Every AI step must bind to a governed prompt contract package.
AI-generated map packages remain draft-only until all governance gates pass.
Mouse Click Ability Group is the only owner of governed mouse click capability.
Mouse Click boundary stays pure.
Mouse Click accepts only pre-validated coordinates.
Mouse Click is enforced by owner inspector and audit runner only.
Mouse Click canonical topology is one primitive-port root with two execution children.
Mouse Scroll Ability Group is the only owner of governed mouse scroll capability.
Mouse Scroll boundary is pure.
Scroll amount and direction are input, not child capability.
Mouse Scroll must emit runtime proof and primitive execution proof.
Nerve Bus is the only owner of governed command transport.
Nerve Bus must not make business decisions.
Nerve Bus is enforced by owner inspector and audit runner only.
Open Ability Group is the only owner of governed open capability.
Open boundary stays pure.
Open contracts must stay replaceable and adapter-neutral.
Open capability is enforced by owner inspector and audit runner only.
Orchestration Ability Group is the only owner of mission command and operational maps.
operational maps are declarative map packages consumed by Orchestration, not child capabilities.
Orchestration dispatches only through Nerve Bus and public ability-group interfaces.
Orchestration is enforced by owner inspector and audit runner only.
Orchestration may request persistence but may not hide round-finalization logic under Forensics.
Orchestration must consume promptContractId from the active approved map and must not hardcode prompt selection.
AI branch decisions must rely only on declared output schema fields.
Orchestration must not build raw prompts.
Page State Ability Group is the only owner of governed current-page state classification.
Page State boundary is pure.
Page State output must be evidence-backed.
Page State must write runtime proof.
Page State must not add dedicated verify script and is enforced by owner inspector only.
platform-action is an Open child sub-contract for platform profiles only, not an active owner.
retained platform profile material must stay finite, auditable, and non-executing.
Post-action Verification Ability Group is the only owner of governed action-result verification.
Post-action Verification boundary stays pure.
Verification must stay unique and traceable.
Post-action Verification is enforced by owner inspector and audit runner only.
Screenshot Ability Group is the only owner of governed screenshot capability.
Screenshot boundary stays pure.
Screenshot artifacts must stay structured and traceable.
Screenshot capability is enforced by owner inspector and audit runner only.
GrassEye must operate only with user-authorized local accounts while minimizing sensitive capture and never bypassing platform security.
Prompt contracts and AI-generated maps must never request sensitive secrets or hidden bypass channels.
Sensitive tasks require review gates before mutating user data or high-risk platform state.
startup-entrypoint is the commander-console bootstrap child sub-contract, not an active owner.
Startup opens Commander Console but does not own Commander Console truth.
Terminal structured logs are display channel only.
startup governance is enforced through the commander-console-capability inspector as a child-contract check.
structured-logging is a Forensics child sub-contract for log discipline, not an active owner.
runtime proof must link to Forensics record refs and may not depend on hidden round finalizers.
DEBUG level runtime transparency must expose what was sent, what was received, and why a decision or failure happened.
every AI model request must emit a structured AI_REQUEST_DEBUG event before the model call.
every AI model response must emit a structured AI_RESPONSE_DEBUG event before parser output is allowed to hide raw model output.
AI failures must report exact cause, actual and max values, missing preconditions, owner responsible, and required upstream action.
user command flow must emit structured debug events from UI command receipt through mission preflight acceptance or rejection.
App shell liveness and mission readiness must be logged separately.
service shutdown and unexpected exits must be classified and linked to last runtime events.
Text Input Ability Group is the only owner of governed text writing capability.
Text Input is write-only capability, not cognition, targeting, gesture, or verification truth.
Text Input accepts only approved text payloads and verified target handoff.
Text Input executes only through governed input, clipboard, and clock ports.
Text Input success is primitive write success only and never verification truth.
Text Input enforcement closes through owner inspector and audit runner only.
Text Input canonical topology is one standard package with six governed execution children.
all external uncertainty must become validated domain types before it can drive actions or records.
Visual Target Ability Group is the only owner of governed visual target result normalization.
Visual Target boundary stays pure.
Visual Target consumes governed evidence and returns typed contracts.
Visual Target is enforced by owner inspector and audit runner only.
